sections.heading: Learning Point 1
sections.content: A Journey through States of Water 8 Chapter On a bright summer afternoon, Aavi and Thirav enjoy their shikanji (lemonade).
sections.source_evidence: A Journey through States of Water 8 Chapter On a bright summer afternoon, Aavi and Thirav enjoy their shikanji (lemonade).

sections.heading: Learning Point 2
sections.content: After looking at the ice in the lemonade, Thirav wonders about the nature of ice and water.
sections.source_evidence: After looking at the ice in the lemonade, Thirav wonders about the nature of ice and water.

sections.heading: Learning Point 3
sections.content: If it does not rain well, even the mighty ocean will be drained. (Thirukkural) We can put water in the freezer of a refrigerator and check if it gets converted into ice.
sections.source_evidence: If it does not rain well, even the mighty ocean will be drained. (Thirukkural) We can put water in the freezer of a refrigerator and check if it gets converted into ice.

sections.heading: Learning Point 4
sections.content: Ice feels hard to touch and we can hold it in our hands, whereas, water cannot be held in the same way.
sections.source_evidence: Ice feels hard to touch and we can hold it in our hands, whereas, water cannot be held in the same way.

sections.heading: Learning Point 5
sections.content: Yes, I know when water is left in the freezer, it gets converted into ice but probably something gets added to the ice in the freezer.
sections.source_evidence: Yes, I know when water is left in the freezer, it gets converted into ice but probably something gets added to the ice in the freezer.

sections.heading: Learning Point 6
sections.content: Curiosity | Textbook of Science | Grade 6 144 Activity 8.1: Let us observe   Put an ice cube in a cup, leave it on the table and observe.
sections.source_evidence: Curiosity | Textbook of Science | Grade 6 144 Activity 8.1: Let us observe   Put an ice cube in a cup, leave it on the table and observe.

sections.heading: Learning Point 7
sections.content: What can you conclude from the observations?
sections.source_evidence: What can you conclude from the observations?

sections.heading: Learning Point 8
sections.content: Does this mean that ice and water are the same substance?
sections.source_evidence: Does this mean that ice and water are the same substance?

sections.heading: Learning Point 9
sections.content: Yes, ice and water are the two forms of the same substance.
sections.source_evidence: Yes, ice and water are the two forms of the same substance.

sections.heading: Learning Point 10
sections.content: These different states of water show many differences in their behaviour.
sections.source_evidence: These different states of water show many differences in their behaviour.

sections.heading: Learning Point 11
sections.content: 8.1 Investigating Water’s Disappearing Act It is a rainy morning.

sections.heading: Learning Point 12
sections.content: While going to school, Aavi and Thirav observe that there are a lot of water puddles in the playground.

sections.heading: Learning Point 13
sections.content: That evening, when they go to play, they are surprised to observe that some of the water in the puddles had disappeared.
sections.source_evidence: That evening, when they go to play, they are surprised to observe that some of the water in the puddles had disappeared.

sections.heading: Learning Point 14
sections.content: Have you ever noticed water in the puddles disappearing?

sections.content: Where else have you seen water disappearing?

sections.heading: Learning Point 16
sections.content: Can you think of a possible reason why this happens?

sections.heading: Learning Point 17
sections.content: You might have observed that after washing the utensils, water left on the surface of the utensils, dries up after some time.
